research.note: Research completeness and decision-evidence sufficiency are intentionally separate.

dimensions.evidence: Defense proliferation, commercial constellation deployment, responsive missions and mission-critical communications support multi-year demand.
Dedicated small launch is supply-disciplined by failures, while medium lift and D2D/NTN are supply-rich / capital-intensive.
Mission-specific dedicated launch and assurance can command premiums, but rideshare and multi-vendor procurement cap universal pricing power.
Rocket Lab is moving from components toward spacecraft prime/mission integration and, if Iridium closes, recurring network services.
Falcon 9 is a powerful incumbent in medium lift and D2D/NTN is attracting large amounts of capital.
Government demand is durable but procurement is multi-vendor and transaction/network economics depend on regulatory and contract outcomes.
Iridium’s differentiated mission-critical L-band use cases are durable, but D2D/NTN can change parts of the connectivity market.
Demand, backlog and revenue growth are visible; cash conversion, financing and dilution determine how much reaches per-share value.

leading_indicators: Neutron qualification → first flight → repeat cadence
SDA/MDA/Space Force milestone delivery and program margin
Iridium subscriber/service growth, EMSS economics and next-gen capital plan
Combined diluted share count and net debt

facts: Gross margin rose from 21.0% in 2023 to 34.4% in 2025; Q2 2026 Launch Services GM was about 42.9%.
counter_evidence: Operating income and FCF remain negative.

facts: Revenue and gross profit scale rapidly across acquired capabilities.
counter_evidence: Acquisition-level organic/incremental ROIC is not disclosed and recent assets are early/loss-making.

facts: Defense spacecraft, responsive launch, Neutron and satellite services provide multiple funded/qualified growth lanes.
counter_evidence: Runway is capital intensive and execution bottlenecks are substantial.

facts: Backlog is contractually defined and gross margin has improved.
counter_evidence: 1H26 CFO -$134.4M; receivables, contract assets and inventory rose sharply.

facts: June 2026 cash plus marketable securities were about $2.39B after large ATM raises.
counter_evidence: Iridium acquisition can add substantial debt and/or equity dilution.

facts: $2.356B backlog, government programs, repeat launch customers and prospective recurring Iridium services.
counter_evidence: Space Systems FFP execution and launch demand remain milestone/lumpy; acquisition has not closed.

facts: Qualification, mission integration and repeat dedicated launches create switching frictions.
counter_evidence: Government concentration is high and multi-vendor procurement is deliberate.

facts: Dedicated launch and mission assurance can command premiums vs rideshare for specific jobs.
counter_evidence: Rideshare, procurement competition and mature satcom alternatives cap universal pricing power.

facts: Acquisitions have assembled an increasingly integrated capability stack.
counter_evidence: Deal-level returns are not yet separable; Iridium is transformative and expensive relative to standalone reference values.

facts: Equity capital was raised at elevated prices, improving liquidity.
counter_evidence: 1H26 ATM gross proceeds $1.53B, note conversions, remaining ATM capacity about $1.944B, preferred and transaction shares expand the denominator.

facts: Enterprise revenue/gross profit growth is strong.
counter_evidence: Weighted-average shares grew and FCF/share remains negative; acquisition financing outcome is unresolved.

business_quality.summary: Strong reinvestment runway coexists with weak cash conversion and dilution discipline; no composite score is used.

forecast_calibration.reason: 8Q pattern largely at upper end / above.

variant_perceptions.market_consensus_view: Backlog and revenue growth can support a premium growth valuation.
variant_perceptions.our_view: Revenue/GP growth is real but per-share value depends on working capital, FCF and dilution.
variant_perceptions.why_mispriced: Growth headlines are easier to observe than program-level cash economics.
variant_perceptions.why_persistent: Program-level Space Systems cash margin is not disclosed.
variant_perceptions.why_converge: 2026–2028 delivery, margin and working-capital data will reveal conversion quality.
variant_perceptions.wrong_signal: Revenue/GP scales and OCF/FCF still fail to improve through 2028.

variant_perceptions.market_consensus_view: First-flight progress can unlock major medium-lift optionality.
variant_perceptions.our_view: First flight is necessary but mature reuse/cadence/cost/ASP/GM drives execution value.
variant_perceptions.why_mispriced: Technical milestones are more salient than mature unit economics.
variant_perceptions.why_persistent: No flight history or mature cost disclosure exists yet.
variant_perceptions.why_converge: First and repeat flights plus cadence evidence in 2026–2029.
variant_perceptions.wrong_signal: Repeated redesign/failure or no credible repeat-flight path by end-2027.

variant_perceptions.market_consensus_view: Recurring Iridium cash flow diversifies Rocket Lab and vertical integration can create synergy.
variant_perceptions.our_view: Standalone cash flow does not automatically become RKLB per-share cash flow after purchase price, financing, dilution and refresh capex.
variant_perceptions.why_mispriced: Strategic fit is visible before retained per-share economics are measurable.
variant_perceptions.why_persistent: Permanent financing and synergy retention are primary-source ceilings.
variant_perceptions.why_converge: Financing disclosure, closing and post-close FCF/share evidence in 2027–2030.
variant_perceptions.wrong_signal: Diluted FCF/share deteriorates despite acquired cash generation.

variant_perceptions.market_consensus_view: Rocket Lab may retain a high-growth scarcity multiple.
variant_perceptions.our_view: Iridium adds a mature/capital-intensive mix that may normalize the blended multiple.
variant_perceptions.why_mispriced: Capital-market identity can remain anchored to high-growth space/tech peers.
variant_perceptions.why_persistent: 2031 business mix and growth durability are unresolved.
variant_perceptions.why_converge: Growth duration, combined margins, FCF and capital intensity become observable into 2028–2031.
variant_perceptions.wrong_signal: Combined growth/margins remain high enough to justify scarcity multiples for longer.

scenarios.name: Execution Break / Deal Friction
positive_updates: Electron/current core exists and is flight-proven
Backlog is enforceable under disclosed accounting definition
negative_updates: Permanent Iridium financing remains a primary-source ceiling
Working-capital and fixed-price-program cash conversion remain weak/uncertain

scenarios.name: Core Executes + Conservative Integration
positive_updates: Quarterly revenue and gross-margin guidance have been well calibrated
Iridium adds recurring service cash flow if transaction closes
negative_updates: Permanent financing mix and cost remain unresolved
Space Systems program-level cash margins are not disclosed
Iridium replacement cycle becomes material around 2031

scenarios.name: Integrated Scale
positive_updates: Defense customer validation and spacecraft-prime position are strengthening
Launch + spacecraft + service vertical fit is economically plausible
negative_updates: Neutron has no orbital heritage yet
Acquisition-level ROIC and retained synergy are not proven

scenarios.name: Platform Upside
positive_updates: Multiple growth engines could reinforce one another if execution succeeds
High Rocket Lab share price can be valuable acquisition currency
negative_updates: Requires simultaneous success across launch, spacecraft, network and financing
Dilution and capital intensity must remain constrained despite rapid scale

kpi_tripwires.current: 93rd Electron mission; 14 launches in 2026 through Aug. 21
kpi_tripwires.green: Cadence stays at/above recent record pace with reliability intact and repeat bookings convert to launches.
kpi_tripwires.yellow: Multi-month schedule slippage or cadence falls below prior-year pattern without demand explanation.
kpi_tripwires.red: Repeated mission failures or a sustained multi-quarter cadence decline.

kpi_tripwires.kpi: Neutron qualification → first flight → repeat cadence
kpi_tripwires.current: Stage 1 qualification remains the gating milestone; first-flight target has moved repeatedly.
kpi_tripwires.green: Qualification closes, first orbital flight succeeds, and a second vehicle/cadence path becomes visible.
kpi_tripwires.yellow: Slip into 2027 with a specific, bounded technical fix and intact customer demand.
kpi_tripwires.red: Repeated redesign/failure with no credible repeat-flight path by end-2027.

kpi_tripwires.kpi: Space Systems backlog conversion / margin / cash
kpi_tripwires.current: Q2 segment revenue $189.5M; GP $65.5M; backlog $1.416B; working capital elevated.
kpi_tripwires.green: Backlog converts while segment margin stays resilient and working capital normalizes.
kpi_tripwires.yellow: Revenue converts but margin compresses or working capital remains structurally elevated.
kpi_tripwires.red: Repeated FFP charges/delivery failures plus worsening cash conversion.

kpi_tripwires.green: Revenue/GP growth begins producing sustained OCF improvement and working-capital reversal.
kpi_tripwires.yellow: Operating growth continues to consume similar cash intensity.
kpi_tripwires.red: Revenue/GP scale materially but FCF remains deeply negative through 2028 without a temporary program explanation.

kpi_tripwires.current: ~639.3M economic-equivalent current denominator before transaction shares; 1H26 ATM and note conversions were material.
kpi_tripwires.green: Iridium permanent financing limits incremental equity and produces a credible deleveraging path.
kpi_tripwires.yellow: Material ATM/equity issuance but at favorable pricing with clear cash-return rationale.
kpi_tripwires.red: Share count grows materially faster than gross profit/FCF per share or financing is expensive enough to crowd out core investment.

kpi_tripwires.current: Q2 revenue $225.2M; 2.627M billable subscribers; service 72% of revenue.
kpi_tripwires.green: Service/subscriber growth remains positive and EMSS successor preserves attractive economics.
kpi_tripwires.yellow: Subscriber/service growth flattens or government economics soften moderately.
kpi_tripwires.red: Sustained service contraction or materially adverse EMSS renewal.

kpi_tripwires.current: Low-capex period expected through at least 2031; extended forecast U-FCF drops to -$21M in 2031.
kpi_tripwires.green: Next-gen plan is staged within combined cash generation and internal launch/manufacturing creates measurable savings.
kpi_tripwires.yellow: Capex rises earlier or larger than expected but remains financeable.
kpi_tripwires.red: Major capex pull-forward or architecture cost causes liquidity/financing strain.

falsifiers.statement: If Space Systems/Electron revenue and gross profit keep growing but cash conversion does not improve by 2028, current-core quality is falsified.
If credible repeat cadence and unit-economics evidence is still absent by 2028–2029 after first flight, remove a large portion of Neutron execution value.
If permanent financing plus transaction shares cause diluted FCF/share to deteriorate despite standalone Iridium cash generation, acquisition value creation is falsified.
If observable cost, schedule or revenue advantage is not visible by 2029–2030, keep ecosystem value near zero.
If Iridium next-gen spending is materially pulled forward or exceeds combined cash-generation capacity, reset terminal leverage and multiple assumptions.
